functional_requirements.requirement: Widen the existing signal-receipt write site to every worker /signal row (not just stuck+high) and render a disposition line, with an existence-check bound sized to the full batch
functional_requirements.description: QF-20260906-162 shipped writeSignalReceipts() in scripts/fleet-dashboard.cjs, gated to payload.signal_type==='stuck' AND payload.severity==='high', with its receipt-existence-check bounded at .limit(50) on the premise that printInbox()'s .limit(20) batch could only ever produce 1-2 stuck+high rows. Remove the stuck+high filter so every worker signal in printInbox()'s enumerated batch gets one signal_receipt row via dispatchToWorker, still correlation_id-idempotent. Since removing the filter widens the batch toward the full 20, the existence-check bound MUST be derived from the enumerated batch's own length (e.g. Math.max(highStuckSignals.length, 50) or paginate via fapPaginate), never a fixed literal that a future batch-widening could exceed -- the same rule FR-5(d) imposes on its gauge applies here at the write site itself. Add a rendered disposition line ('queued' | 'routed:<target>' | 'needs-decision:<who>') into the outbound row's Subject or Details text -- coordination-inbox.cjs's render (line 822 Subject, line 823 Details) has no generic payload-field render, so the line must go in one of those two fields, not a bare payload key. Add 'signal_receipt' to INFORMATIONAL_KINDS (lib/fleet/worker-status.cjs) alongside its existing BACKPRESSURE_EXEMPT_KINDS membership -- this is a DELIBERATE dual membership (classifyCoordinationRow checks INFORMATIONAL_KINDS before the drain-set union, so the kind classifies informational despite also being drainable via the exempt-kind spread) and is the SAME dual-membership pattern signal_receipt already has today; it is not an accident to guard against here, only to record. Adam-advisory receipts and coordinator_request rows are explicitly OUT of this FR: coordinator_request rows carry no payload.signal_type and cannot appear in printInbox()'s signal_type-filtered batch at all (widening the enumeration query to include them is a separate, unscoped change flagged by the code's own comment that it would surface 105+ unrelated INFO rows), and Adam-advisory widening remains cut per the LEAD-phase deletion audit (unbounded duplicate-write risk, filed as a follow-up QF).
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: a worker signal of any signal_type/severity enumerated in writeSignalReceipts' input batch produces exactly one signal_receipt row correlated to it, verified by calling writeSignalReceipts directly with an injected client (its own docblock: extracted specifically for direct unit testability, unlike printInbox which takes no client) and asserting a second call with the same batch writes zero additional rows

AC-2: the receipt row's rendered Subject or Details text (per coordination-inbox.cjs's actual render, not the payload object) contains one of 'queued', 'routed:', or 'needs-decision:' as a literal substring

AC-3: signal_receipt is present in BOTH lib/fleet/worker-status.cjs INFORMATIONAL_KINDS and BACKPRESSURE_EXEMPT_KINDS, and a stub-supabase test with 3 pre-existing unanswered rows on a target plus a new signal_receipt send does not trigger DISPATCH_SEND_BACKPRESSURE_REFUSED

AC-17: a batch of 20 enumerated worker signals (exceeding the old literal 50-row existence-check bound's original 1-2-row premise) still writes exactly one receipt per signal, with zero duplicates, when the existence check is re-run against the same 20-row batch

AC-18: the INFORMATIONAL_KINDS+BACKPRESSURE_EXEMPT_KINDS dual membership for signal_receipt (and any future kind added the same way) is confined to an explicit, named allowlist constant, so an unintentional future overlap between the two lists fails a CI assertion rather than passing silently

functional_requirements.requirement: Replace the dead target_session='broadcast' capped-pool-broadcast mechanism with a per-live-seat directed fan-out, deduped by emission recency rather than acknowledgement state
functional_requirements.description: The originally-specified target_session='broadcast' sentinel has zero worker readers. Build a new module (lib/coordinator/capped-pool-broadcast.cjs) that: (a) reads the live worktree count via countActiveWorktrees()/MAX_WORKTREE_COUNT (lib/worktree-quota.js, ESM, imported dynamically from the CJS coordinator tick); (b) when over cap for more than 30 minutes (configurable), enumerates live seats via liveFleetSessions() (lib/fleet/live-fleet-sessions.cjs) and sends ONE directed INFO row per seat, all sharing one run_id, payload.kind='capped_pool_broadcast'; (c) adds capped_pool_broadcast to PAYLOAD_KINDS, INFORMATIONAL_KINDS, and BOTH copies of BACKPRESSURE_EXEMPT_KINDS (lib/coordinator/dispatch.cjs:39's Set AND lib/fleet/worker-status.cjs:229's frozen array -- two separate constants, both must be updated) plus the corresponding role_drain_sets migration (since BACKPRESSURE_EXEMPT_KINDS is spread into every role's DRAIN_SET, making the kind ackable/drainable by every seat -- this is why the dedupe design below CANNOT use acknowledged_at); (d) DEDUPES FIRE-ONCE ON EMISSION RECENCY, NOT ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: because the kind becomes drainable and any seat can ack its own copy, an acknowledged_at IS NULL dedupe (the emitReaperStarvationAlert pattern) would self-clear the instant one seat drains its row, causing a duplicate broadcast on the very next tick even though nothing changed. Instead, dedupe by selecting whether a row of the same kind for that target was created within the re-emit window (created_at > now - 6h), using the reaper-tick-style state file (scripts/fleet/worktree-reaper-tick.cjs readState/writeState) to track the over-cap-since timestamp and the last-emitted-at time per run, independent of any seat's ack state; (e) emits one additional 'cleared' notice (payload.cleared=true discriminator on the same kind) the first tick the condition resolves, using the same recency-based dedupe.
acceptance_criteria: AC-4: with a live worktree count above MAX_WORKTREE_COUNT for a simulated 31 minutes, exactly one directed INFO row per currently-live seat is produced, and a second tick within the 6h window produces zero additional rows for the same condition
AC-5: when the over-cap condition clears, exactly one additional per-seat notice is sent on the next tick, and zero further notices after that

AC-6: tests/unit/fleet/drain-set-registry.test.js's exact seed-row-count assertion (106 -> 110) and tests/unit/fleet/drain-sets-adam-reconciliation.test.js's per-role count assertions are updated to the new totals and pass; the new migration is added to RECONCILIATION_MIGRATION_PATHS

AC-19: a target that has acknowledged (drained) its capped_pool_broadcast row still receives ZERO additional broadcast rows on the next tick within the re-emit window -- the dedupe is provably independent of any seat's ack state, not merely untested against it

functional_requirements.requirement: Land QF-20260904-724's resolveHoldProvenance key-widening as an exported, precedence-explicit, release-check-aware prerequisite for FR-4
functional_requirements.description: FR-4's CONSTRAINTS block depends on resolveHoldProvenance (lib/fleet/claim-eligibility.cjs:718) correctly resolving a hold's reason text. Widen its precedence chain to also resolve, in this exact slot order: human_action_note and human_action_reason (free-text, inserted immediately after the canonical requires_human_action_reason, since all three are the same 'human must act' hold class), human_action_required (a boolean flag with NO reason text -- synthesize the literal string 'human action required', mirroring how pilot_throwaway already synthesizes 'pilot throwaway venture' for a boolean-only flag), and needs_coordinator_review_reason (inserted immediately after review_hold_reason, since both are the same 'review' hold class, a different semantic category from the human-action class above). NONE of these four new keys has a paired set-at field in current usage, so isHoldReleased()'s release check is explicitly SKIPPED for all four (they resolve unconditionally once present; only the pre-existing requires_human_action_reason and review_hold_reason keys retain release-check gating). Export a HOLD_REASON_KEYS constant (the full ordered list of every reason-shaped key resolveHoldProvenance checks, including the four new ones) so a drift-detection test can diff it against reality instead of re-deriving the list. A reason-shaped key is defined literally as: any strategic_directives_v2.metadata top-level key matching /_reason$/ or in an explicit named allowlist (human_action_note, human_action_required) -- the drift test asserts every such live key is a member of HOLD_REASON_KEYS, MINUS an explicit known-benign exclusion list for keys that are reason-shaped by name but intentionally not hold-provenance (e.g. dedup_judgement, coordinator_review_note if it is not a hold gate). The live-DB scan half of the drift test runs in vitest's opt-in 'db' project (or behind the existing describeDb helper, tests/helpers/db-available.js) since it is inherently DB-dependent and must not run under the default unit tier; the pure resolver logic (given a metadata object, does it resolve the right key in the right precedence) is covered separately at the unit tier with no DB dependency.
acceptance_criteria: AC-7: resolveHoldProvenance(metadata) returns a non-null reason for metadata carrying only human_action_note, only human_action_reason, only needs_coordinator_review_reason (three separate cases, real reason text each), and for metadata carrying only human_action_required=true (returns the synthesized 'human action required' string)
AC-8: the 5 SDs named in QF-20260904-724 (or their current-state equivalents) resolve to a real reason via formatHoldProvenance(), not 'no reason recorded', when re-measured against the live table

AC-9: a unit-tier test asserts HOLD_REASON_KEYS (the exported constant) contains all nine keys (5 pre-existing + 4 new) in the documented precedence order; a SEPARATE db-project test (gated behind describeDb) scans live strategic_directives_v2.metadata for any key matching the reason-shaped predicate that is absent from HOLD_REASON_KEYS and the known-benign exclusion list, asserted at zero

AC-20: none of the four new keys is gated by isHoldReleased() -- a test stamping unfenced_at alongside e.g. human_action_note still resolves the reason (unlike requires_human_action_reason, which the release check DOES suppress under the same unfenced_at)

functional_requirements.requirement: Stamp a CONSTRAINTS block on every WORK_ASSIGNMENT dispatch, writing both body fields directly and failing soft on an oversized render
functional_requirements.description: buildWorkAssignment does not exist; the real choke point is insertCoordinationRow (lib/coordinator/dispatch.cjs:1214), which runs three fail-soft stamper guards keyed on message_type==='WORK_ASSIGNMENT'. Add a fourth, stampConstraintsBlock(supabase, row, logger), following the identical fail-soft pattern: resolve the target SD's ratifications_cited, forbidden-framings text, hold provenance via resolveHoldProvenance/formatHoldProvenance (post-FR-3), and any Solomon-ruling text; render as a 'CONSTRAINTS:' block. THE STAMP WRITES THE IDENTICAL RENDERED STRING TO BOTH row.body AND row.payload.body DIRECTLY (never relying on the existing fill-if-absent mirrors at lines 1468 and 1477 to propagate it to the other field) -- dispatch.cjs has TWO such mirrors (payload.body->body at 1468, body->payload.body at 1477), and a caller who set both fields before this stamp runs would leave one copy stale if the stamp only touched one; writing both directly removes the ordering dependency on either mirror entirely. Apply the existing capBodySafe (lib/shared/body-cap.cjs) to the rendered block BEFORE merging it into the body. WHEN capBodySafe REPORTS BODY_TOO_LONG (it returns {value:null, error}, never throws, never truncates): fail soft, exactly like the other three stampers on any other error -- drop the CONSTRAINTS stamp for that dispatch, log a loud warning naming the SD and the oversized-block byte length, and let the un-stamped WORK_ASSIGNMENT insert proceed unblocked. Do NOT throw and refuse the insert (that would contradict the sibling stampers' contract and turn a formatting overflow into a dispatch outage). When no constraint resolves, the block reads 'CONSTRAINTS: none recorded' -- rendered only when the resolver genuinely found nothing (never omitted, and never rendered as 'none recorded' merely because one key failed to match while others were never checked).
acceptance_criteria: AC-10: a WORK_ASSIGNMENT dispatched for an SD carrying metadata.ratifications_cited and a review_hold_reason produces a body containing a 'CONSTRAINTS:' section naming both, verified against the actual inserted row
AC-11: a WORK_ASSIGNMENT dispatched for an SD with no constraint-bearing metadata keys produces a body containing 'CONSTRAINTS: none recorded'

AC-12: for a caller that pre-sets BOTH row.body and row.payload.body before insertCoordinationRow runs, after the stamp executes both fields are byte-identical and BOTH contain the CONSTRAINTS block -- proving the stamp writes both copies directly rather than relying on either fill-if-absent mirror

AC-13: when the rendered CONSTRAINTS block would push the body over BODY_HARD_CAP (4096), the WORK_ASSIGNMENT insert still SUCCEEDS with the un-stamped body and a logged warning (fail-soft), not a thrown error and not a truncated block

functional_requirements.requirement: CI fixtures asserting each mechanism above, plus a zero-asserted unreceipted-signal gauge
functional_requirements.description: Per ratification 49656c8c's preventive-exit-predicate requirement: (a) drain fixtures (extending tests/unit/coordinator/fleet-dashboard-signal-receipt.test.js) per FR-1's ACs; (b) pool-over-cap fixtures per FR-2's ACs, explicitly including the acked-target-still-suppressed case (AC-19); (c) assignment fixtures per FR-4's ACs, including the both-fields-set case (AC-12) and the oversized-body fail-soft case (AC-13); (d) a gauge (extending lib/fleet/outstanding-signals.cjs's existing 'received' predicate, currently bounded at a literal .limit(20)) counting worker signals older than 30 minutes with no correlated signal_receipt row, asserted at zero from the merge commit, with its existence-check query bound derived from the enumerated result set's own length via the existing fapPaginate helper (never a fixed literal), and its fail-soft catch reporting unknown/error rather than a false-pass zero on a lookup failure.
acceptance_criteria: AC-14: `npx vitest run --project unit` passes with the new fixtures included, and the existing 113-test baseline (captured in .artifacts/testing-plan-to-exec-receipts-broadcast-run.json, matching the LEAD-phase artifact byte-for-byte) still passes unchanged

AC-15: the FR-5(d) gauge reports 0 unreceipted signals older than 30 minutes when run against a fixture with N synthetic signals all carrying receipts, reports N (not 0) when the receipts are removed, and reports 'unknown' (not 0) when the query is made to throw

AC-16: tests/unit/coordination/kind-classification.test.js's informational/actionable disjointness assertion still passes after signal_receipt and capped_pool_broadcast are added to INFORMATIONAL_KINDS, AND a new, separately-asserted overlap check confirms that any kind present in BOTH INFORMATIONAL_KINDS and an effective role DRAIN_SET is a member of the explicit dual-membership allowlist from AC-18 (so the existing disjointness test's structural inability to catch this overlap, per its own before-drain-set-union precedence, is compensated by a check that CAN)

test_scenarios.scenario: A worker signal of signal_type='need-sweep' and severity='medium' (previously excluded by the stuck+high filter) is passed directly to writeSignalReceipts
test_scenarios.given: an injected-client call to writeSignalReceipts with a batch containing one signal_type=need-sweep, severity=medium row with no existing receipt
test_scenarios.then: exactly one signal_receipt row is written, correlated to the signal's id, and re-running on the same batch writes zero additional rows

test_scenarios.scenario: A 20-row batch (the full printInbox() cap, not the old 1-2-row stuck+high premise) is passed to writeSignalReceipts
test_scenarios.given: 20 synthetic worker signals of mixed signal_type/severity, none with an existing receipt
test_scenarios.when: writeSignalReceipts runs, then is re-run on the same 20-row batch
test_scenarios.then: the first run writes 20 receipts and the second run writes zero, proving the existence-check bound covers the full batch size

test_scenarios.scenario: A busy target with 3 pre-existing unanswered directed rows receives a new signal_receipt send
test_scenarios.given: a stub target session already at BACKPRESSURE_UNANSWERED_LIMIT (3) unanswered rows
test_scenarios.when: dispatchToWorker sends a signal_receipt-kind row to that target
test_scenarios.then: the send succeeds (not refused), because signal_receipt is in BACKPRESSURE_EXEMPT_KINDS

test_scenarios.scenario: The rendered receipt row is checked for a literal disposition substring against the actual coordination-inbox.cjs render path
test_scenarios.given: a receipt row written with payload.receipt='routed:coordinator'
test_scenarios.when: the row's Subject/Details are rendered via the real coordination-inbox.cjs render function
test_scenarios.then: the rendered text contains 'routed:' as a literal substring

test_scenarios.scenario: Worktree pool is simulated over MAX_WORKTREE_COUNT for 31 simulated minutes with 4 live seats registered
test_scenarios.given: countActiveWorktrees() returns a value above MAX_WORKTREE_COUNT, over-cap-since timestamp is 31 minutes in the past, 4 live seats from liveFleetSessions()
test_scenarios.then: exactly 4 directed INFO rows are inserted (one per live seat), all sharing one run_id, and a second tick within 6h inserts zero more

test_scenarios.scenario: One of the 4 seats acknowledges (drains) its capped_pool_broadcast row before the next tick
test_scenarios.given: the same over-cap condition as TS-3, and one target's row now has acknowledged_at set
test_scenarios.when: the tick runs again within the 6h window
test_scenarios.then: zero additional rows are inserted for ANY seat, proving the dedupe does not key on acknowledged_at

test_scenarios.scenario: Worktree pool count drops back under cap on the tick immediately following an active broadcast window
test_scenarios.given: the prior tick emitted a capped_pool_broadcast fan-out and the condition has now cleared
test_scenarios.then: exactly one cleared-notice row per live seat is sent, and the next tick after that sends zero

test_scenarios.scenario: resolveHoldProvenance is called against metadata carrying only human_action_note, only human_action_reason, only needs_coordinator_review_reason, and only human_action_required=true (four parameterized cases)
test_scenarios.given: metadata objects each carrying exactly one of the four new keys
test_scenarios.then: each returns a non-null reason (the boolean case returns the synthesized 'human action required' string); none is suppressed by isHoldReleased() even when unfenced_at is also present

test_scenarios.when: a unit test asserts its exact contents and order
test_scenarios.then: it contains all 9 documented keys (5 pre-existing + 4 new) in the specified precedence order

test_scenarios.given: live strategic_directives_v2 rows, run only under the opt-in db vitest project (describeDb-gated)
test_scenarios.when: every top-level metadata key matching the reason-shaped predicate is compared against HOLD_REASON_KEYS plus the known-benign exclusion list
test_scenarios.then: zero unrecognized reason-shaped keys are found

test_scenarios.scenario: A WORK_ASSIGNMENT is dispatched for an SD with review_hold_reason set and no other constraint keys, where the caller pre-sets BOTH row.body and row.payload.body
test_scenarios.given: target SD metadata has review_hold_reason='awaiting Solomon review'; the caller constructs the row with both body and payload.body already populated with distinct base text
test_scenarios.then: row.body and row.payload.body are byte-identical after processing and both contain the CONSTRAINTS block naming the review hold

test_scenarios.scenario: A WORK_ASSIGNMENT is dispatched for an SD with zero constraint-bearing metadata keys
test_scenarios.given: target SD metadata has none of the recognized constraint keys
test_scenarios.then: the rendered block reads exactly 'CONSTRAINTS: none recorded'

test_scenarios.scenario: The rendered CONSTRAINTS block for a WORK_ASSIGNMENT would exceed BODY_HARD_CAP (4096 chars)
test_scenarios.given: an SD with enough ratifications_cited/hold text that the rendered block alone exceeds 4096 chars
test_scenarios.then: the insert SUCCEEDS with the un-stamped original body intact and a logged warning naming the SD, and does NOT throw or truncate the block

test_scenarios.scenario: FR-5(d)'s unreceipted-signal gauge is run against a fixture where the correlated-receipt lookup query throws
test_scenarios.given: the receipt-existence-check query is stubbed to reject
test_scenarios.then: it reports an explicit 'unknown'/error state, never a numeric 0

acceptance_criteria: Every worker signal enumerated by writeSignalReceipts receives exactly one correlation_id-idempotent signal_receipt row, regardless of signal_type/severity or batch size, with zero effect on the target's send-backpressure count

The over-cap fleet-wide notice reaches every live worker seat directly, fires at most once per 6h re-emit window regardless of any seat's acknowledgement state, and fires exactly once more when it clears

Every WORK_ASSIGNMENT dispatch carries a CONSTRAINTS block naming every resolvable ratification/hold/ruling on the target SD in both body and payload.body, rendering 'none recorded' only when genuinely none exist, and failing soft (never throwing) when the render exceeds the body cap

QF-20260904-724's resolver-widening lands as an exported, precedence-explicit, release-check-aware prerequisite, with a unit-tier key-list test and a separate DB-tier drift test preventing the same reader/writer-key divergence from recurring
